title: OSPF Summarization: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: A big network can have a thousand routes. Do you really want every router to carry all of them? Summarisation squeezes them into one.

scenes.heading: The postal sorting office
scenes.narration: Instead of listing every street, you list just the city. A summary route replaces many small ones with one big one. On the border between areas, an A B R uses the area range command. At the edge of the network, an A S B R uses summary address. The not advertise keyword hides the summary completely.

scenes.heading: The commands
scenes.narration: Two commands, depending on the job. On an A B R, use area range. On an A S B R, use summary address. And check the routing table.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. The detailed routes stay in the database. It stops the route being installed, not learned. Only A B Rs and A S B Rs can summarise.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva OSPF summarization lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Summaries keep routing tables small. A B R uses area range, and A S B R uses summary address. Detailed routes remain in the database. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva OSPF summarization lab.
